text:
nina: Quick note from today's staging run: p95 spikes when tiny interactive requests arrive during long coalesce windows. Looks like late-join items are waiting on KV warms and blowing the tail.

liam: saw that too. Logs show `queuelet_age_ms` climbing then a wave of `dispatch wait_for_kv=true` entries.

tara: crude idea: a short-lived 'rescue lane' for queuelets older than threshold. Not full microbatching, but a tiny reserved headroom that drains every 5ms.

nina: rescue lane could limit abuse if we cap per-tenant concurrency. Otherwise someone could flood to steal slots.

liam: agree. Suggestion: implement two controls: a soft voucher counter per tenant (replenish rate tied to recent qps) and a per-slice reserved slot budget.

tara: also include a heuristic: only rescue if estimated_kv_miss_prob > 0.3 then trigger prefetch on admission. Prefetch reduces the warmup penalty.

sre-bot: note: add metrics -> `rescue_lane_alloc`, `rescue_prefetch_trigger`, `voucher_balance`.

nina: tradeoffs: better interactivity vs higher token-cost and possible cache churn. We'll need telemetry (tokens_per_request, p99).

liam: rollout plan: feature-flagged + 1% sample for 2h, gather tail, tokens, GPU_util. Abort if p99 regresses or token cost > 5% increase.

tara: implementation sketch: admission checks queuelet_age, voucher, reserved_slots; if pass -> move to rescue lane; else -> normal coalesce. Keep fallback if lane saturated.

nina: tests: synthetic mix of long streaming and tiny bursts; compare baseline, allow-late-join=false, rescue-lane. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token delta.

liam: I'll draft a short RFC and add a simple state for queuelet: pending -> coalescing -> rescue_requested -> rescued.

tara: ok pairing for PoC this week. I'll add lightweight prefetch prototype too.
